text:
Tom: noticed a big traffic shift off us-east-2 this morning and dashboards for that region are mostly empty — GPU node metrics are missing. creating thread.
OpsBot: incident created: INC-2026-0421. severity: high. 
Maya: looking. are we seeing scrape failures or metrics dropped upstream?
Tom: prometheus targets show the us-east-2 node-exporter job went from 300 targets to 0 around 10:05 UTC. kube-state metrics still exist though.
Priya: could be an exporter crash or a relabel change during the autoscaler surge. I just queried kubectl logs on one node: `kubectl -n infra logs node-exporter-xyz` shows repeated "dial tcp: connection refused" to 127.0.0.1:9100.
Jordan: traces also sparse for that region — jaeger agent on those nodes didn't pick up spans after the shift. might be a networking policy applied by the autoscaler or calico route flap.
Maya: checking network policies and calico logs. also checking recent daemonset rollouts: `kubectl -n infra get ds node-exporter -o yaml | grep image` — no image bumps in last 24h.
Tom: I see a flurry of cluster-autoscaler scale-up events at 10:03, then a flurry of node registrations 10:04-10:06 and immediately many terminated at 10:07. suspicious timing.
Priya: suspected root: new nodes come up with an init script that temporarily disables ipv6 and rewrites iptables for pod-cidr; if kube-proxy restarts during that window some local localhost bindings can fail. Ops logs show `systemd: node-exporter.service failed` correlating.
Maya: i'm seeing prometheus scrape job relabel config for node-exporter uses `__meta_kubernetes_pod_node` and a label filter; nodes with names matching the temporary scale names may have been excluded by a regex. that would explain 0 targets.
Elena: impact: hosted API routes hitting dedicated us-east-2 saw increased latency, some failover to us-west-1 triggered but fallback capacity is squeezed. product noticed uptick in 499s.
Tom: immediate mitigation: re-enable the node-exporter pod on existing stable nodes and remove the relabel exclusion. Priya, can you push a hotfix to the prometheus scrape config?
Priya: pushing patch to prometheus-reloader config now. patch diff: ```
- relabel_configs:
-  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node]
-    regex: "temp-.*"
-    action: drop
+ relabel_configs: []  # temporary: remove drop rule to recover targets
```
Tom: reloader applied, prometheus picked up 298 targets for us-east-2 in ~30s.
Maya: restarting node-exporter daemonset on the 3 problem nodes to force proper binding. `kubectl -n infra rollout restart ds/node-exporter` — restart in progress.
Jordan: jaeger agent fix: nodes had JAEGER_AGENT_HOST unset in the bootstrap image. setting env var and daemonset restart restored traces. quick snippet I applied: `env: - name: JAEGER_AGENT_HOST valueFrom: fieldRef: fieldPath: status.hostIP`
OpsBot: alert: prom targets recovered for job=node-exporter (298 -> 298).
Tom: traffic normalized after targets and traces returned, latency dropped back to baseline, no more 499 spikes.
Elena: good, customers on Dedicated reported degraded throughput for ~25m. need postmortem.
Maya: root cause summary: autoscaler churn + relabel exclusion + init-script network timing caused exporters/jaeger to be unreachable; observability pipeline had a blindspot because the relabel rule dropped temp node names and we had no fallback scrape job.
Priya: immediate follow-ups: 1) re-add a resilient scrape job that matches by pod labels not node name 2) add Prometheus alert if job target count drops >20% for >2m 3) update node bootstrap to ensure node-exporter start ordering and healthcheck 4) make jaeger env explicit in AMI.
Tom: filed follow-up tickets in infra backlog: INFRA-842 (scrape resilience), INFRA-843 (prom alerting), INFRA-844 (bootstrap ordering), INFRA-845 (jaeger env).
Elena: timeline + customer impact for postmortem pls. assign owners and ETA for fixes.
Jordan: i'll take INFRA-844 and INFRA-845, 3 days ETA for bootstrap change and AMI bake.
Maya: i'll own INFRA-842 and INFRA-843, working on alerting playbook today.
Tom: thanks all. postmortem draft will be posted to #postmortems and we'll schedule a 30m incident review tomorrow. :rocket:
